title: Citizenship
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 7 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Kenya's trade examples: tea, coffee and flowers out; oil, vehicles and machines in. Global bodies: UN, AU, EAC.

skills.key_step: The child explains why countries depend on each other today.

floor.prerequisite: Names transport networks of Eastern Africa.
floor.question: Name a transport route from Mombasa.
floor.answer: the Northern Corridor or the SGR

board.do: Draw Kenya with arrows out and in.
Wait for tea, coffee or flowers.

misconceptions.repair: Ask where Kenya's oil comes from.

listen_for: A country is weak and begging
misconceptions.repair: Ask who gains from Kenya's tea.

listen_for: Yes, it has offices in Nairobi
misconceptions.ask: Is the United Nations a Kenyan body?
misconceptions.repair: Show the flags of member countries.

misconceptions.ask: Does Kenya export or import tea?
misconceptions.repair: Ex = out, im = in: draw arrows.

checks.question: Why do countries trade?
checks.answer: no country has every resource or skill

checks.question: Name a body through which countries work together.
checks.answer: any of: the UN, the AU, the EAC

skills.key_step: The child tells what globalisation is and its good and bad effects.

floor.question: Why do countries depend on each other?

representations: a phone made in many countries
steps: Say how to reduce the bad.

board.do: Draw a T-chart: good and bad.
Wait for local culture or firms.

misconceptions.ask: Which is a bad effect of globalisation?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what happens to local shops when cheap imports flood in.
Ask which other things link countries.

misconceptions.ask: How can globalisation help a disease spread?
misconceptions.repair: Recall how COVID-19 spread around the world.

misconceptions.ask: How can cheap imports harm local firms?
misconceptions.repair: Compare a local shoemaker with cheap imported shoes.

checks.question: What is globalisation?
checks.answer: the world becoming one connected place through trade, transport, the internet and finance

checks.question: Give one bad effect of globalisation.
checks.answer: any of: loss of local culture, local firms beaten by imports, cybercrime, spread of disease

skills.key_step: The child names qualities of a global citizen and ways to serve the world while loyal to Kenya.
steps: Say how it serves the world.
Say how it stays loyal to Kenya.

board.do: Write: "A Kenyan nurse works for an aid group abroad."

listen_for: No, he must give up his country
misconceptions.ask: Can a global citizen love Kenya?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what Kenyan peacekeepers do for the world.

misconceptions.ask: Who can be a global citizen?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what a learner can do for the environment.

misconceptions.ask: How can a learner in Kenya act as a global citizen without travelling?
misconceptions.repair: List global actions done at home.

misconceptions.ask: How does buying Kenyan-made goods show loyalty to Kenya?
misconceptions.repair: Trace the money from buying a Kenyan product.

checks.question: Give two qualities of a global citizen.
checks.answer: any two of: respect for other cultures, care for the environment, concern for others, honesty, cooperation, being informed

checks.question: Can a global citizen love Kenya?
